pages.source:
Exam Date & Time: 09-May-2025 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  Manipal Institute of Technology, Bengaluru  
  BTech VI Semester  
  End Semester Examination - April / May -2025  
  APPLICATIONS OF AI IN MEDICINE [CSE- 4014]  
Marks: 50                                                                              Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
1)           A machine learning model is used to classify chemical compounds as either cancer-  
  killing or not cancer-killing. Based on its predictions: It correctly identified 85 actual  
  cancer-killing compounds. It mistakenly labelled 15 non-cancer-killing compounds  
  A)      as cancer-killing. It failed to detect 10 cancer-killing compounds, predicting them as  
  non-cancer-killing.  
  It correctly labelled 90 non-cancer-killing compounds.  
  Considering that missing a cancer-killing compound (false negative) could result in a  
  lost opportunity for a potential treatment, while misclassifying a non-cancer-killing  
  compound as effective (false positive) may just lead to wasted lab resources:  
  (4)  
  1. Calculate the precision, recall, F1-score and accuracy for the cancer-killing  
  class.  
  2. Analyse whether the model's recall is sufficient given the higher cost of false  
  negatives.  
  3. Suggest two techniques to improve recall, and explain the possible trade-offs  
  involved.  
  
  
  B)      A pharmaceutical research team is using machine learning to identify potential  
  cancer-killing compounds from a large dataset of chemical structures. The dataset is  
  labelled based on prior laboratory testing and includes both cancer-killing and non-  
  cancer-killing compounds. To automate classification of new compounds, the team  
  chooses to implement a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. As a data scientist (4)  
  on the team, provide a comprehensive explanation of how the SVM algorithm would  
  be applied in this context along with mathematical and geometric intuition behind  
  how SVM separates the two classes and the role of support vectors, maximum  
  margin hyperplane, and how it contributes to the model's robustness.  
  
  C)      Describe the typical neural network configuration.                                           (2)  
2)           Criticize the three major steps involved in data analysis-data preparation, exploratory  
  data analysis (EDA), and modelling.  
  (4)  
  A)  
  B)      Evaluate preprocessing steps for dominant gene prediction using ANN.                         (4)  
  C)      Illustrate how back pointer algorithm is used to minimize the error.                         (2)  
3)           Evaluate the suitability of Naive Bayes for classifying high-dimensional datasets            (4)

with small sample sizes by comparing its strengths and limitations to classifiers such  
  as Support Vector Machines and Decision Trees, particularly in the context of sparse,  
  A)         noisy, or correlated features.  
  
  B)         Determine filter, wrapper, and embedded approaches to feature selection in a  
  machine learning context. Demonstrate how each method performs in terms of  
  computational efficiency, scalability, and impact on model generalization when           (4)  
  working with high-dimensional datasets.  
  
  C)         Explain how improper use of cross-validation can affect the performance evaluation  
  of a machine learning model. What are some common mistakes and their                     (2)  
  consequences?  
  
4)              Analyse the architecture and learning process of a Deep Belief Network (DBN),  
  detailing the role of each layer.  
  (4)  
  A)  
  B)         Evaluate the effectiveness of the structured workflow used in the review of Clinical  
  Decision Support (CDS) system papers.                                                    (4)  
  
  C)         Explain the process of identifying location of nuclei using haematoxylin stain.          (2)  
5)              Evaluate the effectiveness of high-level NLP components in handling medical  
  applications.  
  (4)  
  A)  
  B)         Analyse the components of an Intelligent Personal Health Record (IPHR) system and  
  how these components interact to support personalized healthcare management.      (4)  
  
  C)         Summarize the main functions and benefits of using an IPHR.                              (2)  
  
-----End-----
